scope: Interpolation/approximation; deterministic and randomized integration; MLMC; numerical SDE rates; optimization and inverse-problem interfaces for statistical computation.

supplies: Generic interpolation, quadrature, random-integration and solver-error contracts.
Abstract MLMC complexity and separately qualified numerical SDE rates.
Convex optimization and inverse-problem contracts reusable by statistical consumers.
consumer_owned: BCS retains posterior/Laplace approximation, inferential calibration and the full statistical error ledger.
MSF-26 retains its natural-cubic and Sobolev spline approximation proof.
ML-58/60/61 retain exact-flow and learned-score/model claims; P-NUM-ODE-01/02 own generic ODE error theorems.

contracts: For distinct real nodes x_0,...,x_n, I_n f=sum_j f(x_j) ell_j, ell_j(x)=product_{k!=j}(x-x_k)/(x_j-x_k), is the unique degree-at-most-n interpolant.
For f in C^(n+1)[a,b], at each non-node x, f(x)-I_n f(x)=f^(n+1)(xi_x)/(n+1)! times product_j(x-x_j).
For Chebyshev-root or Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes, Lambda_n=||I_n||_(C to C)=O(log n), and ||f-I_n f||<=(1+Lambda_n)E_n(f).
proof_route: Cardinal identities give existence; n+1 roots give uniqueness.
Use divided differences or repeated Rolle for the interpolation remainder.
Bound trigonometric cardinal sums for Chebyshev nodes; use I_n p=p for the best-approximation inequality.
guardrails: A logarithmic Lebesgue bound alone does not give convergence for every continuous f without a rate on E_n(f).
Equispaced interpolation can diverge; Weierstrass density is not arbitrary-node convergence.
coverage.source_limit: ATAP Ch. 2 states uniqueness as known; Ch. 5 proves barycentric evaluation. The sample does not prove the general remainder or Chebyshev Lebesgue bound.

contracts: For f in C^2[a,b] and uniform h=(b-a)/n: midpoint error <= (b-a)h^2||f''||_infinity/24; trapezoid error <= (b-a)h^2||f''||_infinity/12.
For even n and f in C^4[a,b], composite Simpson error <= (b-a)h^4||f^(4)||_infinity/180; the rule is exact through degree three.

For positive d-mu=w(x)dx, finite moments through 2m-1, and positive-definite polynomial inner product through degree m, the m-node Gaussian rule at roots of monic orthogonal p_m has positive weights, degree-2m-1 exactness, and for f in C^(2m) error f^(2m)(xi)/(2m)! times integral p_m^2 d-mu.
proof_route: Midpoint: integrate panelwise Taylor remainder. Trapezoid: integrate piecewise-linear interpolation error and sum.
Simpson: derive weights, verify cubic symmetry cancellation, sum fourth-order Peano/Taylor remainders.

Gaussian: prove simple interior roots by sign changes; divide q=p_m r+s; apply orthogonality and Lagrange interpolation; use exactness on ell_i^2 for positive weights; use double-node Hermite interpolation for the remainder.
guardrails: Owen Ch. 7 states Gaussian exactness/error but does not prove them; root and Hermite steps are local obligations.
Tensor-product Gaussian node counts grow exponentially in dimension.

coverage.topic: Adaptive integration and embedded ODE estimates
coverage.contract: Adaptive Simpson/Richardson and embedded Runge-Kutta estimate local defects and refine; a certified global bound additionally needs a posteriori remainder/defect bounds, stability propagation and controlled arithmetic.
proof_route: Specify estimator, decision rule, termination and floating-point model.
Prove a local remainder bound, propagate it through stability, and account for roundoff.
coverage.source_limit: FNC adaptive Simpson gives an example where actual error exceeds the requested tolerance. Embedded RK tolerance is a target, not a universal guarantee.

coverage.topic: IID Monte Carlo, QMC and RQMC
contracts: For IID Y_i with finite variance sigma^2, the sample mean is unbiased with variance sigma^2/n and RMSE sigma/sqrt(n); the CLT additionally requires sigma^2>0.
Koksma-Hlawka: for finite anchored Hardy-Krause variation on [0,1]^d, absolute QMC error <= star discrepancy times variation.

RQMC needs uniform point marginals, not independent points. A nested uniform scramble of a (0,m,d)-net, base b>=max(d,2), n=b^m, f in L^2 gives Var(I_hat)<= (b/(b-1))^min(m,d-1) sigma^2/n <= e sigma^2/n.
For R independent RQMC replicates mu_r, variance estimate=sum_r(mu_r-mu_bar)^2/[R(R-1)]; it estimates randomization variability, not data-sampling error.
proof_route: Derive IID mean/variance by independence; keep the CLT as separate asymptotic sampling calibration.
Use summation by parts in one dimension and anchored mixed-variation decomposition in d dimensions for Koksma-Hlawka.
RQMC unbiasedness follows from uniform marginals; the scramble-variance proof needs ANOVA components and elementary-interval covariance cancellation.
coverage.source_limit: Owen Ch. 15 cites the multidimensional Koksma-Hlawka proof. Ch. 17 cites the nested-scramble variance, smooth-rate and CLT proofs externally. Unknown discrepancy/variation are generally not empirical error bars.

coverage.contract: For h_l=M^-l T, independent unbiased level estimators, |E(P_l-P)|<=c_1 h_l^alpha with alpha>=1/2, Var(Y_l)<=c_2 N_l^-1 h_l^beta with beta>0, and cost C_l<=c_3 N_l h_l^-1: work for MSE epsilon^2 is O(epsilon^-2) if beta>1, O(epsilon^-2 log^2(epsilon^-1)) if beta=1, and O(epsilon^(-2-(1-beta)/alpha)) if beta<1.
proof_route: Choose terminal level from bias; choose N_l proportional to sqrt(V_l/C_l) under the variance budget; evaluate geometric sums.
guardrails: SDE rates and fine/coarse coupling are separate prerequisites.
Giles's adaptive bias/level stopping is heuristic, not a guaranteed theorem.
coverage.source: Giles (2008), Theorem 3.1 and complete proof, read in full.

contracts: Higham-Mao-Stuart Theorem 4.4: autonomous C^1 drift/diffusion; one-sided-Lipschitz drift; globally Lipschitz diffusion; polynomial local-Lipschitz drift; uniform finite moments of every order for exact solution, step process and continuous interpolation. Then E sup_{t<=T}|X-Y|^2=O(h).

Separate P-NUM-SDE-01 local route: X_0 is adapted at time zero, has E|X_0|^2<infinity and is independent of future Brownian increments; coefficients are Borel in time, globally Lipschitz and linear-growth in state uniformly, and have the stated 1/2-Hölder time modulus with linear growth. Its local interpolation proof gives finite second moments and E sup error squared O(h).

Weak order-one local design: bounded payoff phi; backward u(t,x)=E[phi(X_T^(t,x))] in C^2 time/C^4 space with derivatives bounded by C(1+|x|^q); exact/Euler processes have uniform moments p>=2q+8. One-step expected remainder O(h^2)(1+|x|^(q+4)) telescopes to weak bias O(h).
proof_route: Strong source route: localization, all-order moments, EM interpolation defect, Itô/BDG and Gronwall.
Weak design: conditional Gaussian Taylor expansion through cubic order, odd-moment and backward-PDE cancellation, polynomial remainder and telescoping.
guardrails: Do not weaken Higham-Mao-Stuart to X_0 in L^2 or time-dependent coefficients.
The checked sources do not prove the weak contract; deriving backward-solution regularity is separate.
P-NUM-SDE-01's finite-L2 global-Lipschitz/time-Hölder route is distinct and not an H-M-S corollary.
P-NUM-SDE-01 states the temporal modulus qualitatively; specify its norm and constants in the final theorem before authoring.
The published Itô-integral, isometry and multidimensional Itô suppliers carry AC and standing hypothesis (H) from def-elementary-predictable-brownian-integrand; preserve those inherited premises.

contracts: For C^2 f with mI<=Hessian<=MI on the initial sublevel set and attained minimum, exact-line-search gradient descent objective gap contracts by 1-m/M. Armijo backtracking with alpha in (0,1/2), beta in (0,1) has factor 1-min(2m alpha,2 beta alpha m/M).
Damped Newton for C^2 strongly convex f with Lipschitz Hessian on the sublevel set has a finite damped phase followed by full steps and quadratic convergence.
If f is mu-strongly convex and ||grad f(x_tilde)||<=eta, then ||x_tilde-x*||<=eta/mu; an approximate-gradient error delta changes eta to eta+delta.
proof_route: Use the descent lemma, strong convexity and Armijo accepted-step bound.
For Newton, prove finite decrease away from the solution and use the Hessian-Lipschitz remainder for local full-step acceptance/quadratic convergence.
For approximate gradient, use strong monotonicity and Cauchy-Schwarz.
guardrails: These convex results do not give global optimization for multimodal/nonconvex likelihoods.
An approximate objective/normalizer can be biased even if its approximate gradient is solved exactly.

coverage.contract: With b=A x_dagger+e and Tikhonov inverse A_lambda_sharp, x_dagger-A_lambda_sharp b=(I-A_lambda_sharp A)x_dagger-A_lambda_sharp e separates regularization bias from data perturbation.
proof_route: Substitute b and distribute the regularized inverse.
Keep operator discretization, data error, regularization/truncation, iterative stopping and roundoff as separate terms.
guardrails: Use library convention lambda>0 in ||Ax-b||^2+lambda||x||^2; Hansen's slides use lambda^2.
Discrepancy, L-curve, GCV and residual-spectrum criteria are not universal regularization guarantees.
No parallel statistical inverse theorem is needed.

error_ledger.rule: Compose adjacent target differences with the pathwise triangle inequality. A sum of variances/root-sum-square requires centering, covariance or independence.
separate_terms: posterior/Laplace approximation bias owned by BCS
model/learned-score bias that may persist as step tends to zero
error_ledger.replicates: RQMC replicate estimates quantify randomization uncertainty only, not data-sampling error or model bias.

open_problem_candidate.claim: For fixed dimension d>=3, determine the exact asymptotic order of the smallest star discrepancy achievable by n points in [0,1]^d.
open_problem_candidate.boundary: Published lower and upper bounds do not match. No proof is supplied; represent only with the new op- kind if an open-problem lesson is wanted.
open_problem_candidate.source: Owen, Practical QMC, Ch. 15 discrepancy discussion and cited Roth lower bound.

open_problem_policy: Missing local suppliers in this dossier concern established mathematics, not open problems. The d>=3 optimal star-discrepancy order is genuinely unresolved and optional.
